inputs.source: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System: about 14.2mm US adults with diagnosed COPD. No national incidence count is published
stated equal to prevalence, which sets the engine's carryover to zero, so the penetration is the share of each year's eligible patients started rather than a share of an accumulating pool

GSK states that approximately 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have a blood eosinophil count of 150 cells/uL and above, and that this group represents over a million people (GSK release 2025-05-22, citing GSK Optum Analysis DOF 2024N562932_00 and Mullerova H et al., Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis 2019). So the all-eosinophil exacerbating pool is 1,000,000 / 0.70 = 1,428,571, and 1,428,571 / 14,200,000 diagnosed US COPD adults = 0.1006. That is the OBERON and TITANIA entry criterion

inputs.unit: share of the untreated pool per year
inputs.source: Tezspire's measured class capture, at a 1.0 multiple. Tezspire held 16.94% of the US biologic asthma class in 2024 (13,837 Medicare beneficiaries of 81,661 across Tezspire, Nucala, Fasenra and Xolair), and 11.9% of severe asthma patients are on any biologic (Park et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19, doi 10.2147/JAA.S580937, 2,827 patients, 5.2% at GINA step 4 and 19.6% at step 5). 0.119 x 0.1694 = 2.02% of the pool, solved back through the curve and a 25.4% discontinuation to a peak of 0.02039

price.source: Tezspire (tezepelumab), CMS Part D 2024: $183,765,288 over 6,219 beneficiaries = $29,549. AstraZeneca's own alarmin-axis antibody, the nearest comparator on file by class, route and setting, and its Part B figure agrees at $28,676
